title: Package
body:
(JS) reffers to the external manifestation (i.e some code) of a [[Module]]

In practice a package is a directory containing code plus a `package.json` manifest describing it: its name, its version, its entry point, and the other packages it depends on. That manifest is what makes it distributable — it's the unit npm installs, versions, and resolves dependencies for, whereas a module is the unit your code actually requires.

So the relationship is: one package ships one or more modules. `require("express")` names a package; what comes back is the module it exposes as its entry point. Installing one pulls in its whole dependency tree, which is why `node_modules` gets so large and why `package-lock.json` exists — to pin exactly which versions were resolved so every machine builds the same thing.
